column2: Mix the chicken with yogurt, oil and thyme and leave in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Thread the chicken and peppers onto skewers and bake at 200°C for about 20–25 minutes.
Chicken with yogurt
1 teaspoon red pepper flakes
Dice the chicken small and cook it through in oil.
Mix the yogurt with crushed garlic in a separate bowl.
Let the cooked chicken rest for 3 minutes and combine with the yogurt sauce.
Drizzle with lightly heated red pepper oil.
Chicken and vegetable casserole
500 g diced chicken thigh
1 eggplant
Preheat the oven to 190°C; chop the vegetables to the same size.
Put the chicken and vegetables in the casserole; add the oil and water and stir.
Bake covered for 40 minutes, then uncovered for 15 minutes.
Serve when the chicken’s internal temperature reaches 74°C.
Chicken meatballs
500 g minced chicken
3 tablespoons breadcrumbs
Grate the onion and squeeze out the juice; chop the parsley.
Knead the minced chicken, egg, breadcrumbs and vegetables.
Shape small meatballs and arrange on a tray lined with baking paper.
Bake at 200°C for about 20–25 minutes, until the internal temperature reaches 74°C.
Chicken wrap
350 g chicken breast
4 lavash flatbreads
Cut the chicken and vegetables into thin strips.
Sauté the chicken first in oil, then the onion and pepper.
Remove from the heat when the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 74°C.
Warm the lavash, fill with yogurt and the chicken mixture and roll up.
Grilled köfte
500 g medium-fat minced beef
2 tablespoons breadcrumbs
1 teaspoon cumin
Grate the onion and squeeze out the excess juice.
Knead the mince, onion, egg, breadcrumbs and cumin.
Rest the mixture in the fridge for 20 minutes and shape into köfte.
Cook both sides on a preheated grill; bring the internal temperature of the mince to at least 71°C.
Baked köfte
500 g minced beef
Preheat the oven to 200°C; cut the potatoes into wedges.
Knead the mince, grated onion, egg and breadcrumbs and shape into köfte.
Place the köfte and the oil-tossed potatoes on the tray.
Bake for about 30–35 minutes; the köfte should reach an internal temperature of at least 71°C.
Türlü with meat
400 g diced beef
Sear the meat in a pot with a little oil until browned.
Add the onion and soften; add hot water and cook the meat for 35–45 minutes.
Add the chopped potato, eggplant, zucchini and tomato.
Cook for about 25 more minutes until the vegetables and meat are completely tender.
Meat sauté
500 g diced beef
Stir-fry the meat in a hot pot with oil for 5 minutes.
Add the onion and peppers and sauté for 5 more minutes.
Add the grated tomato and hot water.
Cook covered over low heat for 35–50 minutes until the meat is tender.
Chickpeas with meat
300 g diced beef
2 cups boiled chickpeas
Brown the meat in oil; add the onion and fry.
Add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute; add hot water.
Cook the meat for 35–45 minutes until tender.
Add the boiled chickpeas and simmer for 15 more minutes.
Zucchini with minced meat
300 g minced beef
Fry the onion in oil, add the mince and cook until it is fully browned.
Cut the zucchini into half-moons and add to the pot.
Cook covered for 20–25 minutes until the zucchini is soft.
Spinach with minced meat
Wash the spinach in plenty of water and chop roughly.
Fry the onion in oil; add the mince and cook through.
Add the tomato paste and spinach and stir until it wilts down.
Add the water and cook covered for 12–15 minutes.
Potatoes with minced meat
Sear the meat in oil until browned.
Add hot water and cook covered until the meat is tender.
Add the onion, pepper and sliced mushrooms.
Sauté for 12–15 more minutes until the mushroom liquid evaporates and the meat is fully cooked.
Peas with meat
400 g minced beef
Dice the eggplants and soften them in the oven at 200°C with a little oil for 20 minutes.
Fry the onion, add the mince and cook through.
Add the tomato paste and grated tomato and simmer for 10 minutes.
Combine with the eggplants and bake for 10 more minutes.
Bulgur with meat
Sear the meat in oil and add the chopped onion.
Add hot water and cook for 35–45 minutes until the meat starts to become tender.
Add the diced potato and carrot.
Cook for 20–25 more minutes until the vegetables and meat are completely tender.

Baked salmon
4 salmon fillet slices (about 150 g each)
1 lemon (juice and grated zest)
2 cloves garlic (finely chopped)
1 teaspoon dried thyme
Half a bunch dill (finely chopped)
1 teaspoon salt
Half a teaspoon black pepper
Preheat the oven to 200 °C (fan 190 °C) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Rinse the salmon with cold water and pat dry with paper towels; place skin side down on the tray.
In a small bowl mix the olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, garlic, thyme, salt and pepper.
Brush the sauce evenly over the salmon and let rest for 10 minutes.
Bake the salmon on the middle rack for 15–18 minutes, until the flesh flakes easily with a fork and the internal temperature is 63 °C.
After taking it out of the oven, sprinkle with dill, rest for 2 minutes and serve.
For thick fillets extend the time by 3–4 minutes; thin fillets cook in 12 minutes.
If you take the salmon out of the fridge 15 minutes before cooking, it cooks more evenly.
Serve hot with roasted vegetables, bulgur pilaf or rocket salad.
Keep in a closed container in the fridge for at most 1 day; it can also be added cold to salads.

Grilled sea bass
2 portion-sized sea bass (cleaned, 350–400 g each)
1 lemon
3 sprigs fresh thyme or 1 teaspoon dried thyme
1 small red onion (for garnish)
Half a bunch rocket (for garnish)
Wash the sea bass inside and out and pat dry; make 3 diagonal cuts in the skin on each side.
Rub the fish inside and out with salt, pepper and 2 tablespoons olive oil; place 2 lemon slices and the thyme sprigs in the cavity.
Heat a grill pan or barbecue grill well over high heat and oil the grill with the remaining oil.
Place the sea bass on the grill and cook without moving for the first 5–6 minutes; turn with a wide spatula once the skin releases easily.
Cook the other side for 5–6 minutes; the fish is done when the flesh along the back comes away easily from the bones.
Transfer to a serving plate with onion rings and rocket and squeeze lemon over it.
If the grill is not hot enough the skin will stick; wait until the grill starts to smoke before adding the fish.
Using two spatulas to turn the fish keeps it from breaking apart.
Serve immediately with rocket-onion salad, roasted peppers and lemon wedges.
Grilled fish should not be kept; if there are leftovers, remove the bones and refrigerate for 1 day.

Baked sea bream
2 portion-sized sea bream (cleaned)
2 medium potatoes (thin rings)
1 red onion (thin rings)
1 tomato (sliced into rings)
2 cloves garlic (sliced)
Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Spread the potato and onion rings in a baking dish, toss with 1 tablespoon olive oil and a pinch of salt and pre-bake for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile pat the bream dry and make 2 cuts on each side; rub inside and out with salt, pepper and the remaining olive oil.
Place the garlic slices, parsley stems and 2 lemon slices in the fish cavities.
Place the tomato rings on the pre-baked potatoes and the bream on top.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until the flesh on the back comes away easily from the bone; sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve.
Pre-baking the potatoes lets them soften without the fish drying out.
The fish is done when its eye turns white and bulges out.
Serve with the potatoes and tomatoes underneath and a green salad on the side.
Keep in a closed container in the fridge for at most 1 day.
Ba-3-unique-4
Trout with vegetables
2 trout (cleaned)
1 carrot (julienned)
1 zucchini (julienned)
1 red pointed pepper (thin strips)
1 small onion (thinly sliced)
Preheat the oven to 190 °C; prepare two separate large pieces of baking paper.
Toss the carrot, zucchini, pepper and onion with 1 tablespoon olive oil, thyme and half a teaspoon salt.
Spread half of the vegetables in the middle of each paper; rub the trout with salt and pepper and place on the vegetables.
Drizzle the remaining olive oil over the fish and place 2 lemon slices on each.
Fold the edges of the paper to make closed parcels and place them on a tray.
Bake for 22–25 minutes; open the parcel carefully, keep your face away from the escaping steam, and serve.
Cooking in paper lets the fish steam in its own juices and keeps it from drying out.
Cut the vegetables thinly so they cook in the same time as the fish.
Open the parcel on the plate and serve with boiled potatoes or bulgur pilaf.
Keep in the fridge for 1 day; it is better eaten cold than reheated.
Ba-4-unique-5
Whiting with lemon
500 g whiting fillets
4 tablespoons flour
1 lemon (juice)
1 clove garlic (crushed)
2 tablespoons chopped parsley
Pat the whiting fillets dry with paper towels and season with salt and pepper.
Dredge the fillets in flour and shake off the excess.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat; arrange the fillets in one layer and cook each side for 2–3 minutes until golden, then transfer to a plate.
Lower the heat, add butter and garlic to the pan and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the lemon juice and boil for 1 minute, scraping the bottom of the pan; add the parsley.
